review_issue_summaries.summary: Sibling modules import each other through the package __init__ facade, creating an import cycle that depends on import order
Language/override configuration flows through module-level globals and lazy caches, making utils behavior depend on Controller call order
Archive-DB aggregate computation (SQL, rain-event, day extremes) is implemented inside the WeeWX Controller service
utils.py mixes unrelated responsibilities (metadata caches, unit system enum, key-name guessing, value converters, lambda registry)
Sibling modules import via the package __init__, forcing a fragile import order and isort suppression
Language and overrides are process-global state set by Controller, with downstream caches that are never invalidated
Some modules import siblings via the package namespace (relying on __init__ import order with isort disabled), others via direct submodule paths
StationInfo.validate_time_zone omits @classmethod unlike sibling pydantic validators
Optional/Dict from typing in models vs PEP 604 unions and builtin generics elsewhere
WeewxHAController.__init__ returns early after config failure, leaving a half-initialized service whose shutDown() dereferences unset attributes
Locale/YAML load failures are swallowed into {} while utils raises RuntimeError on unreachable None checks
Double logging on config validation and missing exception chaining / traceback in a few handlers
process_packet is reused by three classes with different contracts (transform dict, publish state, discover config returning bool)
Controller future callbacks check_config_update and preprocessor_complete hide that they dispatch follow-up work
get_key_config/get_key_config_dict and get_unit_metadata/_get_unit_metadata_dict differ only by a suffix or underscore
Local variable txBatteryStatus is camelCase in an otherwise snake_case module
utils.py relies on module-global lazy caches that depend on locale_loader globals set elsewhere
utils.py is a catch-all mixing unit enum, metadata guessing, enum lookup and conversion lambdas
Conversion lambdas take an unused config_publisher parameter
setuptools declared as a runtime dependency but never used by source
Submodules import sibling symbols from the package root, forming a cycle with __init__
weewx is imported at runtime but only pinned (==5.1.0) in the test extra; runtime lower bounds have no upper bounds
_augment_db_derived is a long, repetitive method with a nested closure, boolean-flag helper calls and a catch-all except
Executor submit + add_done_callback(check_future_errors) repeated five times, with getattr guards for partially-built state
Function-local import of get_key_config_dict sits beside an existing top-level import from the same module
unit_system None checks and unreachable RuntimeError guards are leftover defensive code; lazy caches use mixed styles
No-op constructor and unused lambda parameter exist only to satisfy shape
DB-derived aggregate computation (SQL, key naming, unit-group registration) lives inside the WeeWX Controller instead of a dedicated collaborator
Unit-system conversion is applied independently in ConfigPublisher.process_packet and StatePublisher.process_packet on the same packet
StatePublisher reaches into ConfigPublisher.seen_measurements and passes the whole ConfigPublisher into every convert_lambda
MQTT client starts before publishers exist, forcing getattr guards in callbacks; package __init__ import order is load-bearing
Controller event handlers, init wiring, preprocessor, and config models have no tests
Controller tests bypass __init__ with __new__ and hand-built stubs, coupling to private internals
reset_locale_state fixture duplicated in six test modules instead of conftest
No integration test drives a packet through the full Controller pipeline
get_key_config is typed to return dict but returns None for unknown keys, causing TypeError in dict(...) callers
Three pipeline classes share process_packet with different return contracts (dict, bool, None)
ConfigPublisher/StatePublisher constructors take 4-7 positional params and Optional-vs-required unit_system mismatch
Controller.__init__ silently returns on invalid config, leaving attributes undefined and forcing getattr guards
Credentials applied behind 'if username and password' though config model already mandates both, creating a silent anonymous-connect path
Empty __init__ with docstring and pass, plus entry debug logs, in PacketPreprocessor
Docstring bloat (Parameters None / Returns None) and 'Processing packet' entry logs on trivial methods
Defensive None checks on non-optional values (unit_system, lazily loaded caches)
Unused StationInfo.time_zone/timezone alias remains and is still documented as a configurable option
models/extension_config.py imports UnitSystem from the package root, creating a reciprocal models<->root edge that relies on __init__ import ordering
Locale globals and downstream lazy caches in utils are decoupled: setting language/overrides after first load is silently ignored, with no reset hook
Package init relies on a hand-ordered import list and models import from the package root
Controller mixes MQTT/executor lifecycle with DB-derived aggregate computation; _augment_db_derived is a long repetitive function
Package __init__ re-exports everything and submodules import from the package root, creating a 7-file import cycle held together by isort: off ordering

payload.strategy_summary: Fix the four reproduced defects first, each behind a test verified to fail against the current code, then take only the cleanups that live in files those fixes already touch. Order: the txBatteryStatus fan-out in preprocessor.py, where 7 of 8 battery sensors publish 2..128 against payload_on 1 and can never report low, together with the None-bitmask TypeError that silently drops the whole packet; the disabled Controller, whose early return at controller.py:109 leaves mqtt_client unset for shutDown at :480; the locale caches in utils.py, which make set_language inert and the six duplicated reset fixtures a false guarantee; then the two genuinely dead unit_system guards, the duplicated local import, one from_config_dict coverage test, and the README line that commit 12d9498 left stale. Everything structural is deferred to a follow-up PR in six groups -- import-topology, module-decomposition, api-naming, packaging-and-config, typing-idiom and error-contract -- cut AFTER this PR merges and then rebased, because module-decomposition rewrites the same controller.py and utils.py regions this PR touches. Two earlier conclusions were reversed on evidence and must not be reopened: the three RuntimeError guards in utils.py are type-narrowing, not dead, since removing them adds three mypy return-value errors against a baseline of one; and renaming the _LAMBDA_REGISTRY timestamp entries is a user-visible breaking change, because convert_lambda names are catalogue vocabulary users can reference through the sensors override and an unknown name degrades to publishing a raw epoch with only a log warning. The plan deliberately carries 12 steps across 6 clusters, not 30 across 12: a reviewer should be able to check four defect fixes and their tests without taking anything on trust.
